findings.claim: The regression test purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser never flushes the session, so the user_location FK is never exercised and the test passes with the fix removed.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, the regression test does not protect the fix: someone can delete the native `delete from user_location` in HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation and CI stays green, while purging a location assigned to any user fails in production with a referential-integrity violation at commit. Fix: assign and saveUser, then Context.flushSession()+Context.clearSession(), reload the location, purge it, and flush again before asserting (and assert the user's locations are now empty).
findings.evidence: Mutation probe: removed the two native-delete lines from HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation and ran `mvn -o -B -pl api -am test -Dtest='LocationServiceTest#probeA2*+purgeLocation_shouldDeleteLocationAssignedToAUser'`. The PR's test PASSED. A probe test (probeA2: assign location 4 to user 1, save, flush, clear, purge freshly loaded location 4, flush) FAILED with `ConstraintViolation ... Referential integrity constraint violation: FK... PUBLIC.USER_LOCATION FOREIGN KEY(LOCATION_ID) REFERENCES PUBLIC.LOCATION(LOCATION_ID) (4)`. With the fix restored, probeA2 PASSED. So the fix is correct, but only a flushing test can detect its removal. Files restored with git checkout.

findings.claim: The new comment says a User.locations collection already loaded in the session just shows stale data. In fact, if that collection is initialized and holds the purged location, the next flush fails with TransientPropertyValueException. The PR's own regression test sets up exactly that case, so the 'no caller holds a loaded User' assumption is false.
findings.evidence: Probe test probeA (the PR's test body plus Context.flushSession() after purgeLocation) failed at the flush line with `IllegalState org.hibernate.TransientPropertyValueException: Persistent instance of 'org.openmrs.User' references an unsaved transient instance of 'org.openmrs.Location' [org.openmrs.User.locations -> org.openmrs.Location]`. The same sequence in a fresh session (probeA2) passes. Suggested fix: do the cleanup through the ORM, for example `select u from User u join u.locations l where l = :location` and then `u.getLocations().remove(location)` before session.remove. That keeps the session consistent and avoids the native bulk update, which with no synchronized query space also invalidates the second-level cache regions. At minimum, correct the comment so it describes a flush failure, not stale data. Production reach is unclear: it needs the user's assignment collection initialized in the same session as the purge.

findings.claim: Because an empty assignment set means unrestricted, purging a restricted user's only assigned location quietly makes that user unrestricted. They then see every tagged location. Retiring the same location instead leaves them with an empty list. Is widening access on purge intended?
findings.evidence: HibernateLocationDAO.deleteLocation removes the user_location rows. Probe probeA2 asserted getUser(1).getLocations().size()==0 after purge and passed. UserServiceImpl.getAllowedLocations returns `tagged` (every tagged location) when `assigned.isEmpty()`. LocationServiceImpl.getLocationsByTag uses dao.getAllLocations(false), so a retired assigned location drops out of the intersection, giving an empty list. The ticket defines empty = unrestricted but says nothing about purge.

findings.claim: getAllowedLocations only requires GET_LOCATIONS. It reloads any user by id through dao.getUser, which skips the GET_USERS check, so a caller with location-read rights can find out any other user's location assignments. Should it require GET_USERS when the user is not the authenticated user?
findings.evidence: Read UserServiceImpl.getAllowedLocations (line 860: `dao.getUser(user.getUserId())`) and the @Authorized(PrivilegeConstants.GET_LOCATIONS) on the interface method. getUser on the service is the GET_USERS-guarded path. Not exercised with a restricted-privilege user, so this ships as a question.

verdict: Not ready to merge: the purge FK fix is correct, but its regression test cannot fail because it never flushes. It needs a flush/clear before it protects anything.
what_i_swept: Checked the diff stat (8 files, +216/-6) against master...HEAD. Read the full diff, the PR body and the TRUNK-6669 snapshot (acceptance criteria: the table, intersection vs all-tagged, no behavior change when unpopulated; REST is out of scope for core, in webservices.rest#762). Approach: a join table on User modeled on user_role (composite PK, same as user_role) follows the ticket and the sibling mapping. Outward trace: (a) location purge path, LocationServiceImpl.purgeLocation -> DAO, with mutation probes as in F1/F2; (b) user purge with assigned locations (probeB: assign to user 502, flush, clear, purgeUser, flush) passed, because Hibernate removes the owning-side join rows; (c) detached authenticated user (probeC: flush, clear, getAllowedLocations(Context.getAuthenticatedUser(), tag)) returned the correct intersection from the DB; (d) @Independent mutation probe: removing it makes LocationUtilityTest.getUserDefaultLocation_shouldReturnTheUserSpecifiedLocationIfAnyIsSet and ContextTest.refreshAuthenticatedUser_shouldSetDefaultLocationIfLocationNull fail with LazyInitializationException, so it is pinned; (e) Envers: User/Location are @Audited and EnversAuditTableInitializer auto-migrates *_audit tables, so there is no hand-written audit DDL to miss; (f) getLocationsByTag excludes retired locations; (g) ran DatabaseUpdaterDatabaseIT (917 count) and ValidateHibernateMappingsDatabaseIT under -Pintegration-test on the default H2 DB, and both passed; (h) the native-delete precedent is HibernateConceptDAO.deleteSubclassConcept (createNativeMutationQuery); (i) one existing @Authorized on an impl method (UserServiceImpl:648), so the impl annotation follows convention.
could_not_verify: DatabaseIT tests were run only against embedded H2, not MySQL/PostgreSQL containers, so the Liquibase changeset was not applied to a real MySQL/Postgres schema here.
F4 (authorization) was not exercised with a user lacking GET_USERS; it is inferred from reading the code.
F2's production reachability (a session holding an initialized User.locations at purge time) was not demonstrated outside a unit test.
